claims.text: Sit with the back against the pad, the thigh pads against the inner thighs just above the knees, feet on the footrests, and hold the side handles.

quotes.text: Sit on the hip adduction machine with back against the pad, adjust thigh pads against inner thighs above knees, feet on footrests, and grip side handles.
Adjust the machine to the appropriate settings, sit down with your legs outside the pads, and grip the handles.

claims.text: Start with the legs spread only to a light stretch in the inner thighs; avoid an excessive stretch at the start. Motra lists forcing beyond a comfortable range as a common mistake.

quotes.text: Start with legs spread to feel a light stretch in inner thighs; adduct until pads lightly touch without forcing.
Avoid excessive stretch in starting position
Forcing beyond comfortable range

claims.text: Squeeze the thighs together until the pads nearly or lightly touch, pause briefly, then return slowly while keeping tension.

quotes.text: Exhale and squeeze thighs together to bring pads inward until they nearly touch.
Pause briefly at peak contraction to engage inner thighs.
Inhale and slowly return legs to starting position, maintaining tension.

claims.text: Keep the spine neutral and the back flat against the pad; avoid momentum and keep the movements slow to prevent strain. Motra lists arching the back off the pad and using momentum to swing the pads as common mistakes.

quotes.text: Keep spine neutral and avoid using momentum.
Keep back flat against pad
Arching back off pad
Using momentum to swing pads

claims.text: Don't use the machine with an acute hip or groin injury; choose a moderate weight and make sure the selector pin is secure.

quotes.text: Do not use if acute hip or groin injury present
Select moderate weight for form
Use weight selector pin securely.

claims.text: Breathe out as the thighs squeeze together and in on the return.

quotes.text: Inhale during the return to start; exhale as you squeeze thighs together.

claims.text: The machine isolates the inner-thigh adductors (Motra names adductor longus and magnus).

quotes.text: Seated machine exercise isolating inner thigh adductors
Adductor Longus, Adductor Magnus

claims.text: Measured in 16 untrained women: the adduction machine recruited the hip adductors about as well as elastic-band adduction.

claims.text: Tempo: Motra lists a 2-1-2 tempo without saying which phase each digit is; read in the order of its own steps (squeeze in, pause briefly at peak contraction, return) it gives 2 s in, a 1 s pause and 2 s out.

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

plate.viewWhy: The legs move together in the frontal plane (c3), which reads only from the front (census: front). The drawn fault, a too-wide start (c2), also shows from the front.
plate.equipment: Seated hip adduction machine (composed, census R3): seat, back pad, footrests, two leg pads on the inner thighs just above the knees, side handles (c1). Floor line.
plate.start: Seated, back flat on the pad (c4); legs apart to a light inner-thigh stretch (c2); pads on the inner thighs above the knees, feet on the footrests, hands on the handles (c1).
plate.end: Thighs squeezed together until the pads nearly touch (c3); back still on the pad (c4).

mistake.what: Starting too wide: the legs are spread into a deep, forced stretch at the start.
mistake.why: Motra ties keeping the movements slow to preventing strain, against "Using momentum to swing pads", first on its common-mistakes list (c4); momentum shows only as speed, so it cannot be drawn. "Arching back off pad" shows only from the side and "Letting weight stack crash" only as speed. Motra's safety notes warn against an excessive stretch at the start, and "Forcing beyond comfortable range" is next on the list (c2); it shows from the front. No source ranks how common it is.
mistake.rankNote: No source measures how often each fault happens. LR-31 step 2: using momentum to swing the pads (c4). Step 1: no frequency word counts for a fault. Set aside: Brandt's "Decreased hip muscle strength is frequently reported in patients with" (c8) is about patients' strength, not a fault; Motra's "Typical Rep Range" is programming. Step 2: Motra's cue "Keep movements slow to prevent strain" (c4) corrects "Using momentum to swing pads", first on its common-mistakes list, and names harm; no other named fault is tied to harm ("Avoid excessive stretch in starting position", c2, names no harm word; "Do not use if acute hip or groin injury present", c5, names no fault). Momentum shows only as speed, so drawable is false and plate.mistake names the next fault by the same steps (step 3, Motra's list: "Using momentum to swing pads", "Arching back off pad", "Letting weight stack crash", "Forcing beyond comfortable range", "Locking knees at end"): the arched back shows only from the side and the census view is front; the crashing stack is speed; forcing beyond a comfortable range, the deep start stretch (c2), shows from the front. Top fault changed: momentum moves to handlingMistakes[0] and the deep stretch to [1]; plate.mistake is unchanged and drawable changes from true to false.

tells.text: Only a light stretch at the start
Pads nearly touch at the end

tempo.text: Up 2, pause 1 and down 2 read Motra's 2-1-2 (c9) in the order of its own steps: squeeze in, "Pause briefly at peak contraction to engage inner thighs.", return. The page does not say which phase each digit is, so c9 is WEAK (R-PB-3); both 2s hold either way. The 1 s pause sits right after the squeeze, where Motra's brief pause is (LR-33); read in the other order, the middle 1 s would sit at the open start, and the brief pause at peak would still give pause 1 as a drawing convention.

setup.step: Sit with your back against the pad and feet on the footrests.
Set the thigh pads on your inner thighs, just above the knees.
Set the start width to a light stretch, not a deep one.
